Direct-drive printed lead screw

A large-diameter 3D-printed screw couples directly to a NEMA17 D shaft through its integral split clamp. An M3×12 bolt tightens into a hex nut captured underneath, so the clamp does not rely on plastic threads. The bore fits a nominal 5 mm D shaft with a 4.5 mm flat-to-opposite measurement, allowing 0.15 mm clearance before tightening. Insert the nut before fitting the screw to the motor; with the carriage extended, rotate the clamp bolt into alignment with the lid access hole and tighten from above. Two 12 mm threaded bands are built into the carriage, at the rear and toward the front. The middle and extended nose are smooth. Both bands remain engaged across 40 mm of travel, while the screw stays 3 mm inside the retracted output face. The nominal screw is 20 mm diameter with 8 mm lead; female relief is 0.35 mm radial and 0.25 mm axial per flank. The bearing stations are 74 mm apart. All widths retain a 195 mm overall retracted length including the motor and 68 mm height. The longer braces extend rearward beside the motor within that envelope. Choose a 42, 84 or 168 mm output plate; corresponding base widths are 80, 122 and 206 mm. Four upper bearings move outward while the motor and screw stay centered. At 2× and 4×, two lower bearings per station sit symmetrically across the width. The wider bearing spacing is intended to resist twisting about the travel axis; stiffness and load capacity need physical testing.

One rigid adjustable carrier

The 1× version has two lower bearings; 2× and 4× have four, evenly paired across the two stations. All lower bearings attach to one printed carrier with side rails and cross-braces. Four M5×25 bolts engage M5 heat-set inserts to pull it upward. The bearings press onto solid integral axles. The carriage running faces are smooth, without raised side rails to catch small bearing misalignment. All bearing seats retain Ø7.4 mm inner-ring lands and 2 mm outer-ring relief. Solid Ø4.8 mm journals retain the 6.4 mm heads and extended 30° bent tips. The relief cuts and deep root clearance are filled; roots connect directly to the support lands. Test forced head passage on the actual PETG print.

Structural lid and mounting

The lid and recessed screw heads stay within the original 68 mm height. Six fixing points join it to the motor mount and bearing stations. Base-floor patterns are cumulative: 1× has 4 holes, 2× has 8, and 4× has 12. All bores are unthreaded Ø5.5 mm. The four outer holes retain their washer pads; inherited inner holes have Ø10.5 mm, 90° countersinks for flush M5 heads. Blind three-ridge M5 pilots provide four lid mounts and six mounts per side. Mount through the inherited inner holes from above before installing the bearing carrier and carriage. The outer holes remain accessible while assembled. Motor bolts are accessible with the carriage extended. The output flange stays 42 mm tall and widens with the selected variant. All widths retain the central NEMA17 31×31 mm pattern; 2× and 4× also have four outer attachment holes.

Print files

Five printed parts: base with solid axles and longer motor braces, pocketed carriage, shared bearing carrier, structural lid and threaded screw. Rounded cutouts reduce base and carriage volume while retaining the bearing tracks, threaded bands, mounting pads and cross ribs. All parts have individual STL downloads and a source bundle. Geometry checks do not establish load capacity, backlash or print-fit tolerances.
